svg.title: How one piece of work moves from idea to production
svg.desc: Four stages, read left to right. Decide what to build (optional): desk-research, then product-strategy, ending when you commit to an outcome. Shape it: three routes. The short route, the default, is frame-intent, you approve the intent, de-risk-intent, decompose-intent. The longer route is frame-situation, identify-opportunities, diverge-solutions, place-bet, map-capabilities. The supervised loop is frame-intent, G0, de-risk and explore, frame-domain, G1.5, design, architecture and contracts in parallel, threat and reliability review, G2, then an ordered backlog. Every route ends at G3, you commit to build. Build it: work-intake routes the work, new-spec writes the spec and plan, you approve both, work-loop builds with gates and three cold reviews, small low-risk changes skip the spec, and the stage ends at G4 when you merge. Ship it: define-slo optionally, release-loop deploys to a throwaway environment, tests end to end and watches telemetry, a deployed failure goes back to the build loop, and the stage ends at G5 when you approve the production ship. Packs used at any stage: code-intelligence, frontend-engineering and iac-terraform, the tracker and design tool packs, converters, governance-extras, and product-documentation.

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
